query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the room-temperature ductility of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) without compromising their high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance. Earlier studies have explored various strategies, including microstructural design, thermomechanical treatment, and composition modification. Recent findings suggest that adding HCP elements to BCC RHEAs can enhance ductility by lowering dislocation core energy and increasing lattice distortion.
decision.unsolved: Despite progress, the poor room-temperature ductility of RHEAs remains a significant challenge. Further research is needed to develop effective interventions that can improve ductility without compromising other desirable properties.
decision.lever: adding HCP elements to BCC RHEAs
decision.why: This approach has shown promise in recent studies, and modifying the composition to include HCP elements could potentially enhance ductility while maintaining high-temperature performance and irradiation resistance.
